# Discovery routing — where a lesson goes

Read when a task surfaced something new — a fact, a repeated failure, a doc found wrong, a routing
miss — and it needs a durable home. The micro-retro and every retro in
[retro-protocol.md](retro-protocol.md) route through this table.

A conversation did not learn anything durable. A discovery is learned only when evidence and an
explicit disposition become a reviewable change or a tracked handoff — the model remembering it is
not storage, and a lesson that never lands is a lesson the next session re-pays for.

## The table

| Discovery | Threshold | Destination | Form |
|---|---|---|---|
| How-we-work rule proven wrong or missing | Twice — or once for a material safety/authority failure | `AGENTS.md`, or the owning skill/agent body | Imperative rule, via PR |
| Platform or tool fact (host behavior, CLI, API) | Once, verified | The owning skill's reference file (platform facts: the installed `prompt-craft` skill's `references/claude-code-frontmatter.md` resource) | Dated fact with its evidence label |
| Recurring failure a check could catch | Twice, same normalized failure | Validator rule, test, eval case, or guard | Deterministic check + the fixture that fails without it |
| Routing miss (wrong component fired, or none) | Once → eval case; twice → description fix | `evals/routing/` cluster; then the description | Eval JSON first; description edits owe before/after runs |
| Operating procedure for a service | Once | Runbook, via `runbook` | Template slots; "Last verified" moves only on run evidence |
| Doc found wrong or missing mid-task | Once | Fix in the same change when small and in scope; else file the gap | Small diff, or a tracked gap named in the packet |
| Incident narrative | Always | `postmortem`, whose feed-forward routes the residue | Postmortem doc; its distilled line lands in the runbook |
| Operator preference or cross-session state | Once | Auto-memory (file + index line) | Dated, evidence-labeled; update the existing memory rather than duplicating |
| Procedure being re-explained or re-pasted | Third occurrence | New or extended skill | Per the skill-creation doctrine; description edits owe eval runs |
| External practice worth importing | A round's worth | The porting method (README, PORT-001) | Import round with adaptation notes |

Thresholds are deliberate, not decoration: a first occurrence is an anecdote, and promoting
anecdotes is how a store fills with overgeneralized claims. "Twice" means the same normalized
failure — same behavior, same boundary, same expected result — not two vaguely similar complaints.
A material safety or authority failure skips the wait.

## Disposition — silence is not one

Every discovery gets exactly one disposition before the task closes:

- **routed** — the table row's artifact exists or is in the PR;
- **filed** — a roadmap item or the target repo's tracker entry, named in the wrap-up;
- **dropped** — with the reason stated where the caller can see it.

Closing a task with an unrouted discovery is the failure this file exists to prevent. A discovery
outside every row is itself a discovery: proposing the missing row is a how-we-work change and
follows that row's threshold.

## Write gates — why the bar is where it is

- **Observed events only.** No speculative lessons; capture is trigger-keyed, never
  calendar-keyed.
- **Store the rule, not the trace.** Abstract the lesson from its incident before writing it —
  specifics that only re-describe one afternoon transfer badly and stale fast. The incident's
  narrative belongs in its report or postmortem, not the durable store.
- **No self-approval.** Durable-store changes ride PRs and operator review; nothing fetched,
  generated, or asserted mid-task approves its own promotion. Memory writes are the one direct
  channel, so they carry a date and an evidence label, and consolidation re-checks them.
- **Delta edits only.** Add, update, or retire items one at a time. A full-store rewrite is how
  learned context collapses — the compressed version reads fine and has lost what mattered.
- **Encode one, file many.** However much a retro finds, it encodes at most one lesson; the rest
  are filed. Ten simultaneous edits change nothing but the diff size.

Threshold lineage: Anthropic's build-over-time triggers (wrong twice → instructions; third paste →
skill), the promote-after-repetition practitioner rule, and the sre-agents `operational-learning`
disposition map — concepts adapted, text original.
